chunks: And Abdul Wahid ibn Abdullah informed us, saying: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Rabah al-Zuhri narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn al-Abbas ibn Isa al-Husayni narrated to us from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Abu Hamza, from his father, from Malik ibn A'yun al-Juhani, from Abu Ja'far al-Baqir (peace be upon him) that he said:
Every banner that is raised before the banner of al-Qa'im, its owner is a taghut.

key_terms.الْقَائِم: Al-Qa'im (The Riser, title of the 12th Imam)

ai.seo_question: Who is considered a taghut among those who claim leadership before the rise of al-Qa'im?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him) declares that any banner raised before the emergence of al-Qa'im belongs to a *taghut*, a term in Shia exegesis denoting not just tyranny but also false objects of worship or authority that divert allegiance from God. This hadith serves as a critical theological filter during the *Ghaybah* (Occultation), warning believers to scrutinize the claims of various pretenders and political leaders against the ultimate authority of the Mahdi. It reinforces the concept of *Tawhid* in governance, where legitimacy is derived solely from divine appointment rather than mere power or popular acclaim.

en.abdullah-al-shahin: (9) Abdul Wahid bin Abdullah narrated from Ahmad bin Muhammad bin Rabah az-Zuhri from Muhammad bin al-Abbas bin Eessa al-Husayni from al-Hasan bin Ali bin Abu Hamza from his father from Malik bin A’yun al-Juhani that Imam Abu Ja’far al-Baqir (as) had said: “
Every banner that is raised before the banner of al-Qa’im will be of an oppressive arrogant.”
